about: dapp-17, r9, r10: the chain a site with no chain of its own starts on (network_space::site_start_chain_for). space_chain_ids: the space in front's networks in the wallet's list order; last_used: the network the person last put a site on in this space (null: none); account_chains: where the signed-in account holds something or used, most telling first. Read by vela-core (tests/site_start_chain_vectors.rs) and by the extension worker's twin (extension/lib/protocol.js siteStartChain / startChainOf, in src/lib/dapp/protocol.test.ts), so the two cannot drift. Spec 105's line (coordinator, r10): a new site starts only on a network of the space in front, and a page's switch reaches only a network of that space (`switches`: network_space::site_may_switch_to, the worker's switchRefusal) — `known` is every network Vela serves, both spaces; a known network of the other space is refused as that space's, an unknown one as not Vela's. r10 follow-up: each refused switch also says the page's sentence (`message`, the 4902's message: network_space::switch_refusal_message, the en of `connect.browser.switchRefusal.*`, and the worker's switchRefusal word for word) and the status line's corpus key (`status_key`). `space_switches`: what a space switch does to the sites (network_space::sites_moved_by_space_switch, the worker's spaceSwitchMoves) — `to`: the space now in front, `space_chain_ids`: its networks, `last_used`: the network last used there (null: none), `account_chains`, `sites`: every site Vela keeps a network for [{origin, chain_id}], `moves`: the ones that move and where, in `sites`' order.
